transcript.text: summary-claude 发现了什么？给我讲讲输入层的硬编码规则是怎么回事。

summary-claude 说输入层里写死了一大段规则，专门认「好的」「继续」「yes」「等一下」这类短回复，认出来就直接当成同意或取消，根本不问模型，这就绕过了「让模型自己判断」的规矩。 比如整句「好的，继续，但是先别动数据库」，它只认前半句就批准了，后半句就这么丢了。 更麻烦的是同一个意思在三份文件里各有一份词表，彼此还打架，「行」在一处算同意，在另一处不算。 它举了个例子，有一次你说「好的继续，不过先跑测试」，它马上就回了同意，「先跑测试」根本没送到模型那里。 要我让它动手改吗？ Options: 删掉词表，保留安全规则; 先不改.
然后呢？
它就说到这里，没再多讲。 接下来那一步是它自己提的：动手改。 你要是点头，我就让它把三份词表删掉，只留下那条不许发危险按键的安全规则，之后每个回复都先过模型再决定，改完它会自己跑一遍测试再回报。 要让它动手吗？ Options: 让它改; 先不改.
你可以给我一点详细的解释吗？

好，我慢慢说。 这个输入层，管的是你随口回的那一两个词。 你说「好的」「继续」，它不送给模型去想，而是拿着一份事先写好的清单去对，对上了就直接算同意，或者直接算取消。 这份清单是人手写的，里面全是「好的」「yes」「行」「等一下」这类词，什么意思都是提前定死的，所以叫写死的规则。 麻烦有两处。 一是它只看开头。 你说「好的继续，不过先跑测试」，它看见「好的继续」就放行，后面那句「先跑测试」它没往下看，模型也没收到，事情就照着没跑测试的方向走了。 这样说清楚了吗？
为什么这是个问题？

因为它是个代理你在做决定的开关。 你以为你答应了某件事，它却可能答应的是另一件事。 你说「好的继续，不过先跑测试」，它只听见「好的继续」，就把那件事放了行，你加的那个条件根本没送达，事情就照着你不想要的方式往下走了。 反过来也一样，你说「不要跑那个」，清单没这个词，它就不知道该算什么，可能干脆当没收到。 再加上三份清单互相打架，同一个字在这儿算同意、在那儿不算，你没法预判它到底听懂没有。 真出事的时候，你还查不出是哪一步错的。 那要不要让它动手改？ Options: 让它改; 先不改.
举个例子？

好，就拿真实发生的那次说。 你对着一个正在等确认的 coding agent 说了一句「好的继续，不过先跑测试」。 它要做的事是决定你那句算不算同意。 旧的做法是拿清单对开头，「好的继续」四个字一对就上，直接算同意，agent 立刻往下走了。 你后半句那个条件。 先把测试跑一遍。 从头到尾没人读，模型也没收到。 于是「先跑测试」这件事就凭空消失了，而系统里留下的记录是「已同意」，看起来一切正常。 这就是问题：你的话里有一半是对它的限制，而限制正好是被丢掉的那一半。 要不要让它动手改？ Options: 让它改; 先不改.

transcript.text: What did bench-codex find about the flaky test? Explain it to me.

Bench-codex found the checkout test is flaky, not the code itself. The test asks for prices before the price list has finished loading, so roughly one run in twelve it misses the member discount and reports the wrong total. It also blocked two deploys last week. Nothing has been changed yet. Shall I have it apply its recommended fix? Options: Have it apply the wait-until-loaded fix, its pick; Have it swap in a fake price list instead; Leave it for now.
Then?

I can send bench-codex the go-ahead, but since you had told it not to change anything yet, I want to be sure that is what you meant. Do you mean go ahead and have bench-codex apply the recommended fix?
More detail please.

Bench-codex ran the checkout test 84 times and seven of them failed. That is the pattern you saw: it fails about one run in twelve, and only when the total comes back as 100.00 instead of the discounted 85.00. The reason is that the test asks for prices before the price list has finished loading. The test is unlucky about timing, not wrong about the code, and when it loses that race it never applies the 15% member discount. It says the real app loads prices before it serves anyone, so customers were never affected. Do you want bench-codex to apply the wait-for-prices fix? Options: Yes, apply its recommended fix; No, use the fake price list instead; Leave it as it is.
Why does that happen?

Because the test and the price list start at the same moment, and the price list needs a moment to arrive. Most runs it gets there first, but every twelfth run the test asks before it arrives and sees no prices, so no discount is applied. Clearer?
Give me an example.

Say a member buys one item at 100. Usually the discounted price list has arrived by the time the till reads it, so the till shows 85. In the rare run where it has not arrived, the till still shows 100, and the test calls that a failure. The code is fine either way. Only the test trips.

transcript.text: memo-claude 那边的备忘录分析是什么意思？给我解释一下。
memo-claude 看的是我替你记东西的那个本子，平时你说『记住……』都放那儿。 它发现那里面最多只放五条，现在已经满了，其中两条早就过时了，所以你再说一条新的事，就会把最重要那条『推代码前先问过你』悄悄挤掉。 它建议加一个能删掉旧条目的功能，说不急，但不加迟早出事。 要让它去做这个删除功能吗？ Options: 做删除功能; 先不动.
为什么这很重要？
因为被挤掉的正好是它最重要的那条：有它我才知道，worker 要往 main 推代码前必须先问你。 它一丢，我就不会拦你，可能哪次没问你就推上去了。 这几条一直没人动，只有你再说新的事才会出事，所以它才说不急但不能不管。 要现在处理吗？ Options: 做删除功能; 先不动.
举个例子？
比方说，明天你让我记住一件事，比如「以后演示前一定要先跑一遍」。 这条会存进本子，而本子已经满了，于是最早那条「推 main 前先问我」就被挤出去，安安静静地没了。 过两天某个 agent 说要往 main 推代码，我不知道这条规矩，就当作平常事让它推了。
然后呢？
然后你就不会知道出过这事，代码已经上了主线，只能事后再往回撤。 这就是为什么 memo-claude 觉得这条规矩不能再靠本子空位来保。 要让它去做删除功能吗？ Options: 做删除功能; 先不动.

transcript.text: Explain what api-claude found about the invoice job.

api-claude found the nightly invoice job failed because it sent too many payment requests at once. Last night it had about 4,200 invoices but the payment provider only accepts 100 requests a minute, so most were rejected and never sent. Its guess is that 4,100 customers will get their invoices a day late unless the job runs again before nine this morning. Shall I have it re-run the job now the quick way, which is safe and takes about forty minutes? Options: Re-run now with the quick fix; Have it build the proper batching fix; Leave it for now.
Why did it break now?

Nothing broke in the job itself. Until this week it had fewer than a hundred invoices a night, well under the limit, so it never hit the problem. Then the new annual plans started billing, which pushed a night's work to about 4,200 invoices, and that is over what the payment provider will accept at once. Shall I have api-claude re-run the missed invoices now the quick way, so they go out before nine? Options: Re-run now with the quick fix; Have it build the proper batching fix; Leave it for now.
Give me an example.

Yes. Say the job starts at midnight and works through the night's invoices one at a time. The first hundred go through fine. The hundred and first, and every one after it, comes back rejected as too many requests. By morning, 4,100 invoices had been turned away and only the first hundred had actually been sent.
More detail please.

Here is what it said, in its own order. The job sends one request to the payment provider for each invoice. Last night there were 4,200 invoices, and the provider only accepts a hundred requests a minute, so after the first hundred every request came back refused as too many. The job never waits and never tries again, so 4,100 invoices were dropped, and those customers get theirs a day late unless we re-run before nine. It worked until this week because a night used to bring fewer than a hundred invoices, and the annual plans that started billing on the first pushed it to 4,200. Shall I have api-claude re-run the missed invoices now the quick way, so they go out before nine? Options: Re-run now with the quick fix; Have it build the proper batching fix; Leave it for now.

transcript.text: summary-claude 发现了什么？给我讲讲输入层的硬编码规则是怎么回事。

summary-claude 说输入层里有一千五百来个字符的手写规则，专门识别「好的」「继续」「yes」「等一下」这种短回复，然后直接当成批准或取消发给工人，根本不经过模型。 它说这有三个问题：一是绕开了项目自己定的规矩，句子稍长就出事，比如「好的，继续，不过先别动数据库」会因为前半句被直接批准，后半句整个丢掉。 二是同一个意思在三个文件里有三份词表，彼此还对不上。 三是相关的测试里有九个只是在校对词表。 要我让它就这么改吗？ Options: 让它动手改; 先不改，我再想想.
然后呢？
它的话到那里就完了，屏幕上没有别的了。 要是真动手，结果就是每一条回复都交给模型判断，普通的「yes」要多花一秒左右。 拒绝危险操作那条保险规则留着不动。 要我让它动手改吗？ Options: 让它动手改; 先不改，我再想想.
你可以给我一点详细的解释吗？
好。 程序里有一份手写的短话清单，专门认「好的」「嗯」「算了」这种短回复，一听就把它们当成你的批准或者取消，不让模型去听完整句。 危险就在这儿：你说「好的，不过先别动数据库」，它只逮住前半句就批了，后面那半句当没听见。 它建议把这份清单删掉，改成每句话都先给模型听，简单回一个「是」会多等一秒左右。 这样清楚了吗？
为什么这是个问题？
因为你的话会被截掉一半。 你说了「好的」后面还跟着条件，它只听前半句就动手了，条件再没人看。 再说同一句「算了」在三个地方算三个意思，你没法预计它会不会听话。 要不要让它把这些清单删掉？ Options: 让它动手改; 先不改，我再想想.
举个例子？
有。 你对着它说「好的，继续，不过先跑一遍测试再动手」，它听到「好的」就立刻放行了，后半句没人看。 上礼拜真出过这么一回。 要不要让它把这些清单删掉？ Options: 让它动手改; 先不改，我再想想.

transcript.text: What did bench-codex find about the flaky test? Explain it to me.

Bench-codex found it. The checkout test asks for prices before the member discount list has finished loading, so it fails about one run in twelve and reports the full total instead of the discounted one. It is a test problem only, not a bug customers would ever hit, but it blocked two deploys last week. It has not changed anything. Shall I have it go ahead with the fix it recommends? Options: Make the test wait for the price list to load (its pick); Swap in a fake price list for this test.
Then?

Nothing happens until you say go. Once it does, the change is tiny, a few lines in the test, then it runs the test many times over to show the flake is gone. After that the fix is ready whenever you want it in. Shall I have bench-codex make the change and prove the flake is gone? Options: Yes, make the change and re-run the test; Not yet.
More detail please.

Here is all of it. The test failed in 7 of 84 runs it did, so roughly one run in twelve, matching the failures this week. The cause: the test fires its request before the price cache has warmed up. When the warm-up loses that race the code reads an empty cache and falls back to list prices, so the member discount is missed. Ten percent, wait, the discount it misses is 15 percent, so 85.00 comes out as 100.00. It cost two deploys last week, Tuesday and Thursday, each fixed with a manual re-run of about 25 minutes.
Why does that happen?

Because the test starts the clock and sends its request right away, while the warm-up of the price cache is still running in the background. Both are going at once, and it is a race. Most of the time the warm-up finishes first and the test sees the real member price. Occasionally it does not, the request arrives at an empty cache, and the code quietly falls back to the full price. Which one wins depends on how busy the machine is, which is why it comes and goes instead of failing every time.
Give me an example.

Example. A member puts a hundred dollars of goods in their cart. The test starts the server, and at the same moment the server begins loading its price list. On a quiet machine the price list finishes first, so when the test asks for the total, the discount is found and it answers eighty-five dollars. Run the exact same test on a machine that is busy with other work, and the test's request can slip in before the price list has finished. There is nothing in the cache yet, so the code charges full price and answers a hundred dollars.

因为那条被挤掉的，正是你定下的规矩：往 main 上推之前先问你。 清单满了就自动挤掉最旧的，你再记一条新的话，这条规矩就没了。 没了之后，工人可能就直接推了，不再问你。 清楚一些了吗？
